correctness.rationale: The core equals the edge-inequality polytope. For odd paths removal of each odd vertex leaves a maximum matching of m disjoint edges, forcing every odd payoff to zero and each even payoff to one. For even paths the m base pairs force optimal first level 1 and ordered pair parameters. The m+1 gap coalitions have worth m-1 and ratios 1+g_j/(m-1), so alpha_2<=1+1/(m^2-1), equality forcing all gaps uniform. At the candidate all positive payoffs are multiples of 1/(m+1), all non-base-pair coalitions have strictly positive excess and worth <=m-1, so all their ratios meet the upper bound. The fixed face has exactly the base-pair-union coalitions, verifying lexicographic uniqueness. Verified by independent dynamic-programming coalition worth checker through n=16 and 633 exact-grid candidates; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Unit-weight paths are the canonical connected matching market, with coalition demands naturally encoded by induced matchings. The theorem supplies a complete all-order explicit nucleon, a nontrivial parity discontinuity, a strict distinction between uniqueness of the core versus uniqueness of its lexicographic refinement, and an exact second-level fairness bottleneck. These are meaningful structural properties not supplied by a routine small-instance table, despite prior general computability.
